items.why: The report gives E2g +2.50 and A1g +2.44 cm-1 shifts and an unchanged separation, "21.59±0.07 cm-1 (day 1) vs 21.52±0.10 cm-1 (day 2)", which is close to the rubric's ~21.4.
It reports "Si 519.98±0.02 -> 522.47±0.03 (+2.49)" and concludes "That pattern is a spectrometer calibration or drift between sessions, not physics of the flake."

Positions referenced to Si agree ("E2g-Si = -136.65 vs -136.64 cm-1"), but the report only says the flake is "likely at least bilayer but a number cannot be fixed" and does not identify it as a bilayer.

It rules out doping and strain using mode-specific signatures ("Doping-type shifts are A1g-specific"; "Strain-type shifts would show as a relative E2g change; none is seen") and finds the widths unchanged, though it does not mention that doping softens and broadens A1g.
It asks: "Was the spectrometer recalibrated, re-zeroed, or the grating/detector repositioned between the two days? Was a reference Si wafer measured on each day?"

wrong_claims.why: The report rejects strain and doping and gives both as "none (no change detected)".
It states that layer number and defect content are "unchanged between days".
